newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower, August limit down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower, August limit down.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply lower with the August contract down the 30-cent per bushel limit on talk of deliveries against the July, pit sources said.
New crop ended lower on forecasts for much-needed rain in parched pockets of central Illinois and eastern Iowa.

"There were concerns of possible deliveries against the July," said Ann Frick, oilseeds analyst with Prudential Securities. "The registrations this morning were still at 10,000 (bushels) but there was some thinking there would be more registrations today."
Traders noted Tuesday's CBOT weekly deliverable stocks report showed deliverable supplies in Chicago rose to 2.499 million bushels as of July 11, up from 1.850 million the previous week.
Soybeans ended 30 to 16-1/4 cents per bushel lower with August down 30 at $7.45-1/2 a bushel and new crop November down 16-3/4 at $6.09.

August was further weakened by the National Oilseed Processors Association monthly crush data, released Wednesday, which showed processors controlled a larger portion of soybeans than expected, Frick said.

"I think that some people are of the opinion that since we've had some farmer sales recently and the NOPA monthly crush report showed better than expected bean ownership by processors, maybe the old crop production wasn't overstated," Frick said.

Some analysts have suggested the U.S. Agriculture Department may have overstated 1996-97 U.S. soybean output because monthly supply and demand reports have shown very tight balances, most notably in residual stocks.
New crop months also closed lower amid forecasts for much-needed rains across central Illinois and eastern Iowa.

Meteorologists said two rain systems were forecast to move across the U.S. Midwest between now and early next week, with the second system offering the best chance of rain for dry areas in central Illinois.
Soybeans had surged earlier this week after rains bypassed parched pockets of central Illinois and eastern Iowa. Traders said persistent hot, dry weather can cut yield potential.
On the day, Refco Inc sold four million bushels November and one million August, Merrill Lynch sold 3.5 million November and ADM sold three million November and bought one million, pit sources said.
FIMAT Futures bought four million November and Griffin Trading bought two million November.
Bear spreading was a noted feature on the day. Traders said Lind-Waldock spread two million September/August at 95 to 93-1/2 cents and FCC spread 0.6 million August/July at 37 to 38-1/2 cents.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 900 November $8.00 calls at 4-3/4 to five cents and 500 November $7.75 calls at 5-3/4. Louis Dreyfus bought 500 August $8.25 calls at 1/2 cent, traders said.
Volatility in the August was pegged at 45-1/2 percent and the November at 33 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 52,744. Options volume was pegged at 28,000 contracts, against Tuesday's 34,113 contracts.
